source_registry.publisher: Circle Internet Group, Inc. via SEC EDGAR
source_registry.authority: SEC-hosted issuer Exhibit 99.1; primary issuer disclosure
claims_supported: The direct SEC-hosted URL resolves to an EX-99.1 document titled Circle Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results.
Q3 2026 average USDC in circulation was $73.3 billion, up 8% year over year; end-of-period USDC was $73.9 billion, flat year over year.
Q3 USDC on-chain transaction volume was $13.9 trillion, up 49% year over year; this is gross transaction volume, not net new USDC issuance, unique users, XRP volume, or net payment settlement.
Q3 total revenue and reserve income was $864.888 million; reserve income was $657.624 million, down 8%; other revenue was $207.264 million, up 627%, including $182 million from the ARC token presale.
Q3 net income from continuing operations was $226.012 million; adjusted EBITDA under Circle's new definition was $316.662 million.
USDC minted during Q3 was $104 billion and redeemed was $104 billion; these are gross mint and redemption measures, not net issuance.
Q3 end-of-period stablecoin market share was 27%, down 183 basis points; meaningful wallets were 7.3 million, with Circle defining a meaningful wallet as one holding more than $10 USDC.

At September 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents segregated for the benefit of stablecoin holders were $73.574857 billion; deposits from stablecoin holders were $73.451092 billion; cash equivalents segregated for corporate-held stablecoins were $1.016461 billion.
Circle Payments Network annualized total payment volume was $41.3 billion. Circle said it signed a definitive agreement to acquire Tazapay, expected to close in 2027 subject to regulatory approvals.

Tazapay was reported to have more than $25 billion in annualized payment volume, 60-plus banking and fintech partners, local payout rails in 100-plus markets, and approximately 60% of transaction volume already involving stablecoins.
The exhibit says Binance announced a $100 million equity investment in Circle and an expansion and renewal of the USDC strategic partnership across Binance's global platform.
limitations: The SEC-hosted exhibit content was retrieved as rendered web text, not as byte-complete source bytes; no raw SHA-256 receipt is claimed.
The direct exhibit URL resolved, but the separate EDGAR filing-index URL did not resolve in this run; do not claim the filing index was independently verified.
Circle-authored content hosted by SEC EDGAR remains issuer-origin evidence, not independent corroboration of Circle's own claims.
The reported Binance $100 million equity investment is described as announced; closing, funded amount, share class, ownership percentage and beneficial ownership were not independently verified.
Q3 on-chain transaction volume and CPN annualized TPV must not be interpreted as XRP demand or as interchangeable measures.

circle_q3_metrics.meaningful_wallet_definition: On-chain digital-asset wallets holding more than $10 USDC.
interpretation: Average USDC circulation grew, but end-period circulation was flat year over year.
Reserve income fell despite average circulation growth because the reserve return rate declined.
A large portion of the year-over-year increase in other revenue was the ARC token presale; total revenue growth is not a pure measure of USDC reserve demand.
Equal gross USDC mint and redemption totals are not proof of zero net changes in every intraperiod window; they are quarter aggregates and must not be converted into a net capital-flow claim.
The $13.9 trillion on-chain transaction-volume measure is distinct from $13.9 billion USDC on platform at quarter-end.

findings.claim: Circle's Q3 revenue growth cannot be interpreted as a direct proxy for USDC reserve demand: reserve income fell 8%, while other revenue rose 627% and included $182 million of ARC token presale revenue.
Average USDC circulation grew 8%, but end-period circulation was flat year over year; gross minting and redemptions were both reported at $104 billion.
Circle's Q3 exhibit reports that Binance announced a $100 million equity investment in Circle alongside an expanded and renewed USDC partnership; closing and funded capital remain unverified.
The OCC CAS record lists Ripple National Trust Bank as approved on 2025-12-12 and consummated/effective on 2026-10-26; Ripple describes the 2026-10-26 action as final approval.

Ripple states that Standard Custody & Trust Company remains the RLUSD issuer while Ripple National Trust Bank has a separate reserve-management, collateral-trustee and fiduciary-custody role under its approved business plan.

Ripple's $16 trillion product transaction figure, $900 million annualized product revenue run-rate expectation and $150 billion lifetime volume claim are not XRP-specific settlement or capital-flow measures.

Circle's USDC, Arc, Binance distribution partnership, Visa Direct deployment and Tazapay expansion show that stablecoin settlement can scale through rails that do not require XRP; this is a competitive counter-hypothesis, not proof that USDC displaces XRP.

competing_hypotheses.statement: Ripple's institutional product growth may eventually increase XRP demand if payment, liquidity, financing or collateral workflows actually require XRP.
evidence_against: Ripple's product transaction total is not XRP-only.
RLUSD and tokenized money-market-fund rails can settle without XRP in some workflows.
No XRP-specific inventory, payment share, collateral utilization or net purchase data is established by these releases.

competing_hypotheses.statement: USDC, RLUSD and other stablecoin/payment rails may capture institutional settlement activity without requiring XRP as a bridge asset.
evidence_against: Stablecoin use and XRP liquidity can be complementary in corridors where stablecoins need local conversion or XRP is used as an intermediate asset.
The retrieved sources do not measure the XRP share of Ripple Payments or institutional flows.

competing_hypotheses.statement: Circle's Q3 revenue growth primarily reflects higher USDC reserve demand.
evidence_for: Average USDC circulation grew 8% year over year.
USDC on-chain transaction volume grew 49% year over year.
evidence_against: Reserve income declined 8% year over year.
End-period USDC circulation was flat year over year.
Other revenue rose 627%, including $182 million of ARC token presale revenue.

disconfirming_evidence: Circle's Q3 reserve income fell 8% despite average USDC circulation growth.
Circle's end-period USDC circulation was flat year over year and stablecoin market share declined 183 basis points.
A substantial portion of Circle's Q3 other revenue increase came from the ARC token presale, not reserve income.
Ripple's $16 trillion 2025 product transaction figure is not identified as XRP-only settlement.
OCC's consummated/effective status does not by itself prove RNTB customer operations have commenced.
Binance's announced $100 million equity investment is not proof of a completed or funded equity transaction.
